why: A (exists_isEulerNumber) says that a compact nonempty slice submanifold N ⊆ ℝ^{K+1} (dim d+1, K > 0) has an integer χN equal to the index sum of every smooth tangent field with finitely many zeros (zeros given as an injective enumeration). B says the index sum (a finsum over the finite zero set) equals Milnor's χ(N) = Σ_{λ≤d+1} (-1)^λ dim H_λ(N;F) for every field F. B ⇒ A: take χN = χ(N;ℚ) and convert an enumeration to a finsum. A ⇒ B: K = 0 is vacuous (a slice chart forces m = 0, so N is a nonempty compact open subset of ℝ¹: no_K_zero), and for K > 0 the identification χN = Σ(-1)^i b_i(N;F) is the project's IsEulerNumber.eq_sum_bettiNumber (Morse inequalities for L_p, outside the item). So B's homological identification needs substantial project input beyond A, but the two are formally equivalent given it.
overlap: B_to_A: 191 shared, all Milnor.* infrastructure (Milnor.Tub.* tubular-neighbourhood/indexN definitions' auxiliary proofs, SliceChart.toChart, Sphere.*) reached through the definition of indexN, which both statements use; 0 Morse.* theorems, none of the Poincaré–Hopf proof
